questions.question: Two million active writers produce four keystrokes per second, and the client marks 1% of boundaries as eligible. What peak inference rate should the serving tier plan for?
options: 8,000 requests per second
80,000 requests per second
800,000 requests per second
8,000,000 requests per second
questions.explanation: The estimate is 2,000,000 x 4 x 0.01 = 80,000 eligible inference requests per second.

questions.question: A compact replica can serve 2,400 requests per second, and target utilization is 70%. How many replicas are needed for 80,000 requests per second before adding any extra regional redundancy?
options: 24 replicas
34 replicas
48 replicas
70 replicas
questions.explanation: Usable capacity is 2,400 x 0.70 = 1,680 requests per second per replica. 80,000 / 1,680 rounds up to 48 replicas.

questions.question: A suggestion passes language-quality checks but arrives after the draft version has changed. What should the client do?
options: Insert it because model quality already passed
Wait for the user to stop typing and then insert it
Send it to the quality model for another check
Discard it because it belongs to stale composer state
questions.explanation: Freshness is a hard online gate. A good candidate for an old draft can be incorrect at the current cursor and must be discarded.

questions.question: Why should a safety-service timeout produce no generated suggestion instead of bypassing the gate?
options: Normal typing still works, while unchecked generated text could violate a hard guardrail
It always improves acceptance rate
It guarantees the model will use fewer tokens during training
It allows raw email text to remain in logs longer
questions.explanation: Smart Compose is optional, so failing closed protects the hard safety contract without taking down email composition.

questions.question: A candidate improves fleet-wide acceptance but exceeds the unsafe-output gate for sensitive-context mail. What is the correct release decision?
options: Launch globally because the aggregate product metric improved
Launch only to users who accepted the previous model
Hold exposure until the failing safety slice is resolved
Remove the sensitive slice from the report
questions.explanation: A hard safety gate applies to the affected slice. Aggregate acceptance cannot buy permission to expose a known safety regression.

questions.question: Why is an accepted suggestion not automatically a clean training label?
options: Acceptance contains no information about usefulness
The user may edit it, the event is contextual, and reuse still needs a privacy-reviewed data process
Accepted suggestions always violate the latency budget
Only ignored suggestions can be used for evaluation
questions.explanation: Acceptance is one contextual signal, not ground truth or consent for reuse. Edit behavior, sampling, labeling, privacy, and retention controls still matter.

questions.question: Why should rollback restore the model, tokenizer, context schema, and policy as one versioned bundle?
options: It makes every model larger
It guarantees all users receive suggestions
It removes the need for canary testing
Mixing incompatible versions can create incorrect tokens, features, or gate behavior
questions.explanation: The serving contract spans all four artifacts. Rolling back only the model can leave incompatible preprocessing or policy behavior active.
